newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for end to appliance price wars.
newsitem.headline: China calls for end to appliance price wars.

text.p: China's Vice Minister of the Electronics Industry Liu Jianfeng called for an end to price wars in the electric appliances sector and said competition should be based on improved technology.
There have been price wars since the first half of this year in personal computers, VCRs, colour televisions and other products, the Business News on Thursday quoted Liu as saying.
This has caused a drop in profits at firms making colour televisions and their components, a rise in inventories and a shutting down of production at the weaker firms, Liu said.
Overall profits and taxes of colour television firms fell 11 percent in the first half of 1996 from the same 1995 period and their losses mounted, the newspaper quoted Liu as saying.
Thes price wars resulted from an excess of supply over demand, the impact of smuggled goods and inadequate means by the government to regulate the market, he said.
Price-cutting was not the only way to compete, the minister said. He urged firms to improve management, raise the quality and diversity of their products and improve after-sales service.

The Business News reported in a separate story that Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliances Co Ltd expects its 1996 output of colour televisions to reach 4.3 million units, up from 3.052 million in 1995.
This would account for 27 percent of the domestic market, up from 22 percent in 1995.
The company expects 1996 sales to reach 12 billion yuan, up from 6.764 billion in 1995, and to reach 30 billion by 2000, the newspaper said.
